title: Superconducting transmission cable economics
bottleneck: High-temperature superconducting cables can carry 5 to 10 times the power of conventional lines in the same corridor, ideal for dense cities, but require continuous cryogenic cooling, cost far more per mile, and a single cooling failure takes the whole cable offline. Demonstration projects exist but no utility has deployed HTS cable as routine infrastructure.
why_it_blocks: Urban grid congestion is acute and new corridors are politically impossible, yet the technology that could multiply existing corridor capacity remains a laboratory curiosity for cost and reliability reasons.
current_state: HTS cable demos operate in the US, Europe, and Asia. Costs and cooling-system reliability block commercial adoption. Niche deployments near city substations may come first, where the value of corridor capacity justifies the premium.
